draft.title: The Articles of Confederation
card: The Articles of Confederation were the first constitution of the United States. They were written during the war and took effect in 1781.
The states had just broken from a distant, powerful government. They feared another one, so they kept most power for themselves and made the national government weak.
Congress could not tax. It could only ask the states for money, and they often did not pay. It also could not control trade between states or with other countries.
Congress struggled to pay its debts or deal firmly with other nations. Many leaders came to believe that the national government needed more power, and this led to calls for change.
draft.remember: The Articles gave the states the power and left Congress too weak to run the nation.

a.q: Why did the Articles of Confederation give the national government so little power?
opts: States feared a strong central government after Britain
States wanted Congress to control trade between them
Leaders believed a weak government could raise taxes easily
Britain required the new nation to have a weak government
a.why: The states had just broken away from a powerful distant government and feared creating another one, so they kept power for themselves. The option about Britain is tempting, but the weakness was the states' own choice, not a British demand.
a.clue: Think about what the states had just escaped.

b.q: In 1785, Congress needed money to repay its war debts. Under the Articles, what could it do?
opts: Ask the states to give money, which they might refuse
Collect a tax directly from citizens in every state
Charge duties on trade between the states
Order the states to pay and punish any that refused
b.why: Congress could only request money from the states, and they often did not pay. It could not tax people directly. Ordering and punishing states is wrong because Congress had no such power, which was the weakness that led to calls for change.
b.clue: Congress had no power to tax, only to ask.

a.best: States feared a strong central government after Britain

b.best: Ask the states to give money, which they might refuse
